not_claimed: Statewide count of licensed CILA agencies or homes, market shares, named competitors or CILA occupancy/vacancy rates — DHS publishes a provider list (last updated 07/15/2026) [S45], but no official count or occupancy data was verified.

Code-level 2026 CILA rates by individual rate tier — only DDD's floor rates ($129.00 statewide / $147.00 Chicago Metro per day) [S19], the waiver-amendment averages [S15] and the 2025 average topline [S17] were verified. 24-hour CILA rates are individually determined under the approved methodology (Guidehouse methodology, staffing formulas effective 7/1/2024) [S16][S17][S19]. No model should assume a uniform rate.

Whether the $375.11 average daily rate in the waiver amendment [S15] has been reflected in the posted DDD rate table — the amendment is an application document and the figure sits far above the $129.00–$147.00 floor rates.

Whether CILA residential (60D) and intermittent (61H) claims are subject to EVV — the verified EVV scope covers Personal Care Services and Home Health Care Services billed to DDD only [S24][S25]. The 75% quarterly EVV compliance threshold from 4/1/2026 is verified [S24].

Whether DD waiver services are billed fee-for-service through IMPACT or through HealthChoice Illinois managed care — not confirmed from an official DDD/HFS source; only a secondary vendor statement exists.

Illinois-specific IMPACT enrollment fee for CY2026 — only a secondary vendor statement of a federal $750 institutional-provider fee [S61] was found and its applicability to CILA agencies is unconfirmed.
CILA license renewal fee amount — the statute authorizes a fee under 210 ILCS 135/4 but the dollar figure was not located on a primary source.
Current BALC processing time for application review and the initial interview — only the 15-working-day site-inspection window [S3] and the 6-month post-admission site visit [S5] were verified.

Awake-overnight and other staffing ratios in Rule 115 itself — the ratio tables found are rate-bulletin funding definitions [S16], not licensure ratios. Licensure requires on-site staff whenever residents are present unless the Personal Plan says otherwise [S3][S53].
Full administrator / QIDP / Residential Services Director qualifications and current medication-administration training hours — listed on IDHS pages but text not retrieved or outdated.
Host family minimum caregiver age and other host-family details — only a 2005-era BALC document was found.

Agency general liability, professional liability, property or surety-bond minimums for CILA agencies — none found in the Part 115 text retrieved. Insurance premiums in any model are operator estimates.

Illinois-state BLS OEWS May 2025 wages for direct support professionals, LPNs, cooks, QIDPs and managers — the IDES page lists 2025 annual data [S43] but the Illinois wage rows were not retrieved. National BLS figures (RN $101,420; general and operations managers $134,940) [S42] are not Illinois wages and must not be used as Illinois wages.
Whether the pending HB2788 (150% of minimum wage for DD staff) was enacted is unverified [S51]. The Chicago minimum wage of $17.05 from 7/1/2026 is taken from the City of Chicago.

2026 Illinois state unemployment insurance wage base and new-employer rate — secondary sources conflict ($14,250 vs $13,590 vs $13,271; 3.175% / 3.35% / 3.525% / 3.95%); the IDES primary page was not fetchable [S38][S39].

Illinois LLC late annual-report penalty ($100 vs $300 plus $100/month in conflicting secondary sources) and per-class workers' compensation rates — Illinois is an open-rating state with carrier-set rates and secondary sources conflict [S40][S59].

Official 2026 room-and-board dollar amount for CILA residents — HFS says the 2026 Supportive Living Program room-and-board amount is being updated but does not state it [S22]. The $874/month cap (SSI $994 less $120 personal needs allowance) is a secondary-source figure for Supportive Living, not CILA [S23].

Commercial rent or purchase prices for Illinois residential homes suitable for CILA — no survey searched. HUD Fair Market Rent is a 40th-percentile gross rent definition [S44]; the Chicago metro 2BR FY2026 figure ($1,781) is secondary [S60]; no metro-wide 4-bedroom figure was verified.

Current PUNS wait length — the only verified figure ('5 or more years') is from an undated older IDHS page [S29]. A parent-advocacy site cites about 44 months as of March 2025 and a third-party guide estimates about 16,500 on the waitlist; neither reconciles with DHS's 6,367 adult-eligible count [S30].
Referral-source breakdown for CILA admissions, share of CILA capacity filled from PUNS vs. other pathways, ICF/DD census, and FY2026 PUNS selection counts.

Final outcome of the FY26 CILA funding reduction referenced in HJR0044 [S52], and the final enacted FY2027 DDD appropriation — only the proposed $3.2 billion [S48] and secondary summaries [S49][S50] were found.
Status of HB5471 (2026 bill to shorten the license term from 3 to 2 years) [S13] and whether any 2026 amendment to 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115 is pending.
Local zoning and building-code requirements — these vary by municipality. No state-level zoning standard beyond Rule 115.310 was found.
Any profit, break-even point or payer-mix figure — these are computed by the generators from sourced inputs, not claimed here.

Whether a statute caps the CILA application fee at $200 — the $200 nonrefundable fee paid with the application is confirmed by IDHS [S5], but 210 ILCS 135/4(d) was not read, so the cap is not claimed. The renewal fee amount is also unverified.

An Illinois RN wage — the model's $48.76/hour is the national BLS mean, not an Illinois wage. CareerOneStop (BLS May 2025) lists an Illinois RN median of $46.15/hour; the Illinois mean was not retrieved.

Paid leave (Illinois Paid Leave for All Workers Act; Chicago paid leave and paid sick and safe leave ordinance) and overtime premium costs for 24/7 coverage — real employer costs that are not in the payroll burden; amounts were not verified.

The $375.11 average daily rate and the $60.48 intermittent CILA rate (61H) in the 1915(c) waiver amendment — the waiver PDF (IL.0350.R05.04) could not be fetched, so these figures could not be checked against Appendix J.

Size-specific CILA averages ($122,806 / $129,935 / $140,196 for 8-, 6- and 4-bed homes) come from the 6/30/2025 DDD update, before the 1/1/2026 DSP wage increase; current rates for specific residents must be confirmed with a rate letter or the DDD CILA Estimated Rate Calculator.

occupancy.rationale: Share of licensed beds billed each day. No CILA occupancy or vacancy data was found (see not_claimed), so 90% default (85% conservative, 95% optimistic) is an operator assumption, not a sourced statistic. Demand is deep: DHS's 7/1/2026 PUNS snapshot shows 8,985 adults Seeking Services and 6,367 eligible for adult waiver selection [S30]. But adult selections occur only once a year [S28], and people choose a provider through their ISC agency, so a new home fills in steps and vacant beds earn nothing.

configurations.label: One 4-person CILA home, 24-hour, average-acuity residents (average waiver rate)
configurations.notes: The most common small-agency starting model. Revenue uses the 2025 DDD average annualized topline for 4-bed 24-hour homes ($140,196/year, about $384.10/day) [S17]. Rates are set per person under the approved methodology, so an actual rate letter can be far above or below this average. A 4-person home covers its costs only narrowly at the average rate (roughly a 5% margin by approximate recomputation). The owner usually fills the administrator or QIDP role to stretch the margin.

sections.executive_summary:
Illinois does not call this business a 'group home license.' The model is the **Community Integrated Living Arrangement (CILA)**. A CILA is a residential site where **eight or fewer** adults with developmental disabilities live with agency-provided supports [S2][S53]. The agency must hold a CILA license from the IDHS **Bureau of Accreditation, Licensure and Certification (BALC)** under 210 ILCS 135 and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115 [S1][S2][S3]. BALC licensure is the first step before Medicaid waiver enrollment [S1].

**Money flows through the Medicaid HCBS Waiver for Adults with Developmental Disabilities.** HFS is the state Medicaid agency and IDHS-DDD is the operating agency (waiver version IL.0350.R05.04, effective January 1, 2026) [S14][S15]. CILA rates are set under a DDD-designated rate methodology, currently the Guidehouse methodology, whose staffing formulas took effect July 1, 2024 [S4][S16][S17]. **24-hour CILA (program code 60D) rates are individually determined, not a single published rate.** DDD's 2026 rate table shows the lowest rates on file at **$129.00/day statewide and $147.00/day in the Chicago Metro region** [S19]. The 2026 waiver amendment lists a **$375.11 waiver-wide average daily rate** (up from $364.50) [S15], but that average is not specific to home size. DDD's 6/30/2025 update shows average annualized toplines by house capacity: **$122,806 for 8-bed homes (about $336/day), $129,935 for 6-bed (about $356/day) and $140,196 for 4-bed (about $384/day)**, against a 24-hour average of $134,395 [S17]. Room and board is not paid by Medicaid. The resident covers it from income, usually SSI, which is $994/month in 2026 [S22][S63].

**Demand is large but slot-limited.** DHS's 7/1/2026 PUNS snapshot shows 8,985 adults (18+) Seeking Services and 6,367 eligible for adult waiver selection [S30]. Adult selections happen once a year, in order of time in the Seeking category [S28][S31]. Most Ligas class members who entered service chose Home Based Services (7,032) rather than CILA (1,559) [S32]. The waitlist is therefore not the same as CILA demand. A new agency gets no guaranteed referrals. People choose a provider through their Independent Service Coordination (ISC) agency [S28].

**The economics are thin and depend on the individual rate letter.** At the size-specific average rates and 90% occupancy, approximate recomputation shows the 4-person home netting about **$2,400/month (about 5% margin)**, breaking even at about 85% occupancy. The 6-person home nets only about $1,000/month (about 1.6%), breaking even at about 88% occupancy. Three 4-person homes net about $5,300/month (about 4%). **The 8-person home loses about $3,200/month at 90% occupancy** and would need about 94% occupancy to break even. These are approximate figures and the model's startup cash and first-profit-month results must be regenerated at the new rates. **At the floor rates the same homes lose heavily:** about $13,066/month for a 4-person home at $129.00/day and about $15,268/month for an 8-person Chicago-area home at $147.00/day. Whether to enter depends on the rates actually authorized for the residents you intend to serve. This report does not claim them. Unverified items, including the renewal fee, the CILA rate table by individual, insurance minimums, Illinois-specific wages and CILA occupancy, are listed in the 'What This Report Does Not Claim' section.
sections.service_model:
**Who is served.** CILA serves adults with developmental disabilities enrolled in the DDD Medicaid HCBS Waiver for Adults with Developmental Disabilities [S4]. The statute defines a CILA as a setting where 8 or fewer recipients with a developmental disability live under the supervision of the agency [S2]. DHS describes it as a place where eight or fewer people live together [S16]. The rule defines a CILA site as a residential setting certified by the Department with eight or fewer individuals, and a CILA agency as a developmental disability services agency licensed by the Department to provide CILA services [S53].

**Service variants.** DDD's rate model uses program code **60D for 24-hour and host family CILA** and **61H for hourly intermittent CILA** [S17]. Intermittent CILA serves people in their own or family homes, not agency-operated 24-hour sites. This report models only the agency-operated 24-hour home, because that is where a new agency's fixed costs sit. Residents in host family arrangements are treated as needing 24-hour service, and host families may not leave them alone except as the plan specifies [S55].

**Regulatory framework.** Agencies that plan to develop CILAs must do so under Department licensure in accordance with Part 115 [S4]. The governing statute is 210 ILCS 135 [S2][S64]. The rule states its intent as uniform direction for licensure and operation of CILA agencies [S56]. IDHS reports that an amended Part 115 has been adopted by JCAR and is in effect. The amendment adds person-centered planning and conflict-free case management [S46]. The page does not state the effective date. Verify the current text with BALC before drafting policies.

**Setting rules that affect site selection.** A new provider-owned or leased site may not be adjacent to (next to, across from, diagonal to or immediately behind) another Medicaid HCBS waiver-funded residential or day site owned by the same provider unless a waiver is granted [S8]. The waiver request must be filed **before** the agency leases, buys or takes possession of the property [S8]. In a multi-unit building, no more than 25% of units may be CILAs funded by the Department and owned or controlled by CILA providers [S8]. DHS says the old 800-foot spacing rule has been superseded and the proximity limit now targets only provider-controlled CILAs [S9]. Local zoning is separate and varies by municipality. It was not researched (see not_claimed).
sections.licensing_pathway:
The steps below follow IDHS's New Provider Guidance for CILA and Part 115 [S5][S3][S12]. **The licensure rule text and the guidance page do not give a processing time for application review or the initial interview.** Plan on several months before a provisional license and verify with BALC. The only rule timelines verified are listed in the steps.

1. **Confirm eligibility and attend orientation.** BALC releases the application only after verifying eligibility [S12]. Certain prospective providers must attend a BALC New Provider Orientation before they can request the application packet. Some are exempt [S10]. Under Rule 115.410(a)(1), new provider requirements must be fulfilled within one year of requesting a licensure application, so track that deadline.
2. **Request and submit the application.** Request it from BALC (401 S. Clinton, 7th Floor, Chicago, IL 60607; 312-814-5310). The page lists the email as DHS.BALC@illinois.gov, while another IDHS page shows dhs.balc@illinois.gov. Confirm which is current [S1][S11]. Submit the application with the required documents and the **$200.00 nonrefundable application fee**, which is paid with the package [S5]. A statutory cap on the fee was not verified. The application step includes a current electronic fingerprint check for the owner(s), authorized representatives, registered agency and officers or administrator, run through IDPH [S5].
3. **Pass the initial interview, then file the required documents.** After the application is approved, you must pass an initial BALC interview. You then submit policies and procedures, a projected two-year budget, sample case files and sample implementation strategies [S5]. **Failing the interview or the policy review means you may not reapply for one calendar year** [S5]. Treat this as a hard gate and invest in the policy package.
4. **Provisional license.** On completing the application process the Department may issue a provisional license for up to one year, covering one site serving up to eight people [S4]. **DDD enrollment steps cannot be completed until BALC sends notice of a provisional license** [S5].
5. **Site readiness and inspection.** Before a new agency-owned or leased site is occupied, BALC must inspect it. Site inspections are completed within **15 working days** after all necessary documentation, such as current fire clearances, is received [S3]. When the property is ready, BALC asks the Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM) to add it to the inspection list [S5].
6. **IMPACT enrollment.** IMPACT is the Medicaid enrollment and reimbursement system for DDD providers, and federal reimbursement requires enrollment first [S27]. Other enrollment prerequisites to plan for are an FEIN, a Type 2 NPI (taxonomy 320900000X), ROCS/CIRAS enrollment, and DDD approval of the agency's DSP and QIDP training programs after enrollment; confirm each with DDD. The Illinois-specific enrollment fee was not verified (see not_claimed). A secondary source gives a federal $750 institutional-provider fee for CY2026, but its applicability to CILA agencies is unconfirmed [S61].
7. **First admission and permanent license.** BQM makes an unannounced visit within the first year of the first admission [S5]. BALC does a site visit within six months, and a passing agency receives a **permanent license for 3 years** [S5].
8. **Stay licensed.** Agencies must be **operational within 18 months or the Department treats the licensure process as abandoned** [S7]. On Department notice, a signed renewal application is due at least **120 days** before the license expires [S7]. Ownership changes must be reported to BALC and DDD within 60 business days [S7]. The Department conducts unannounced surveys at renewal and for complaints and health and safety concerns [S4]. Every site is inspected at least once during the licensure period [S3]. A secondary report says CILA surveys occur every two years [S62].

**Term discrepancy to watch.** The guidance page says 3 years [S5], while the rule text on inspections refers to a two-year period of licensure [S3]. HB5471 (introduced 2/13/2026) would change the term from 3 years to 2 years. Its status is not verified [S13]. Ask BALC what term applies to your license and budget renewal costs accordingly. The renewal fee amount was not located on a primary source, and the model carries a $25/month placeholder (operator estimate) [S6].
sections.reimbursement:
**Payer structure.** HFS is the state Medicaid agency and IDHS-DDD is the operating agency for the Adults with Developmental Disabilities 1915(c) waiver [S14]. The waiver version in effect from January 1, 2026 is IL.0350.R05.04 [S15]. CMS accepted three DD waiver amendments addressing FY26 budget increases (DDD communication of December 10, 2025) [S21], and DDD says I/DD rates take effect January 1, 2026 [S20]. ICF/DD rates were still pending CMS approval of state plan amendments as of the December 2025 communication [S20]. HFS lists a further proposed waiver amendment effective 01/01/2027 [S14]. **Whether waiver services are paid fee-for-service through IMPACT or through managed care was not confirmed from an official source.** Only a vendor blog says IL Medicaid uses FFS via IMPACT alongside managed care plans [S61]. Confirm your billing path with DDD.

**How the CILA rate is set.** CILA services are funded through the rate methodology DDD designates [S4]. The older individual rate determination model has been retired and current rates use the **Guidehouse Rate Methodology** [S16]. The Guidehouse staffing formulas took effect July 1, 2024 [S17]. DDD's January 1, 2026 rate table says the 24-hour CILA rate is **individually determined under the approved CILA rate methodology** [S19]. A regional wage and rate factor applies to CILA and Community Day Services. The Chicago Metro region is Chicago plus Cook, DuPage, Kane, Lake, McHenry and Will counties [S19].

**Rate benchmarks (none is a rate you can assume).**
- **Floor of rates on file:** $129.00/day ($47,000/year) statewide and $147.00/day ($53,700/year) in Chicago Metro [S19]. DDD notes that actual rates are usually higher.
- **Average toplines by house capacity (DDD 6/30/2025 update):** 8-bed $122,806/year (about $336.46/day), 6-bed $129,935/year (about $355.99/day), 4-bed $140,196/year (about $384.10/day), against a 24-hour average of $134,395/year (about $368/day) [S17]. These predate the 1/1/2026 DSP wage increase, so confirm against a rate letter or the DDD CILA Estimated Rate Calculator.
- **Waiver-wide average in the 2026 amendment:** the 24-hour CILA average daily rate rises from $364.50 to $375.11 [S15]. This is a waiver-wide average across individually determined rates, not specific to home size, and the model does not use it as a per-home rate. The amendment is an application document, and it was not verified that the posted rate table reflects it.
- **Administration allowance:** the 6/30/2025 update reports an average annual administration allowance of $14,385 per 24-hour person (the 2024 update showed $13,764) [S17][S18].
- **Intermittent CILA (61H), 1 person:** $60.48, up from $59.09 statewide [S15]. Confirm the unit in the DDD rate table.

The model uses the size-specific averages ($384.10/day for 4-bed, $355.99 for 6-bed, $336.46 for 8-bed) at 30.42 days per month for the average-acuity cases. It shows the floor rates as stress tests. **Get the rate letter or rate determination for each resident before committing.** The Chicago floor is $18/day above the statewide floor, but the home still loses money (see Section 8).

**Room and board.** Medicaid does not pay room and board in any state [S63]. HFS reports the 2026 maximum SSI for a single person is $994 [S22]. A secondary source gives a Supportive Living cap of $874/month ($994 less a $120 personal needs allowance), but that program is not CILA and no official CILA amount was verified [S23]. The model assumes $600/month collected from each resident as an operator estimate that leaves spending money.

**Wage pass-through.** DDD requires CILA provider agencies to certify that wage increases are passed through to direct care staff [S47]. Keep payroll records that tie each rate increase to wages.

**Budget direction.** The FY2027 proposed budget includes over $3.2 billion for DDD, and state spending on I/DD community services is cited at about $2.5 billion in FY2026 [S48]. A secondary advocacy summary says the final FY2027 budget, passed May 31, 2026, includes a $0.60/hour DSP increase [S49]. Another secondary analysis of the proposal says there is no overall increase to regular CILA funding [S50]. A legislative resolution says the FY26 budget eliminated $11.2 million for CILA providers. The final outcome was not verified [S52]. Treat the funding direction as uncertain.
sections.demand:
**What the waiting list shows.** PUNS is the database that registers people who want or need DD Waiver services such as CILA and Home Based Supports. Enrolling is the first step to waiver services [S28][S31]. The DHS 7/1/2026 snapshot shows 14,971 people in the Seeking category and 2,983 in Planning across all ages. For adults 18+ it shows 8,985 Seeking and 1,885 Planning, and 6,367 adults eligible for adult selection [S30]. Wait-time bands among adults seeking services include 956 people (15%) at 36 to 47.99 months, 1,951 under 12 months and only 2 at 60 or more months [S30]. Only 46 seekers are aged 65 and over [S30].

**How people get in.** Selection is based on cumulative time in the Seeking Services category, and enrollment does not guarantee services [S28][S31]. **Adult waiver selections occur once a year** [S28]. People facing homelessness, abuse or neglect are told to notify their ISC agency promptly and may qualify without waiting for selection [S28]. Individuals enroll through ISC agencies, which are the intake and referral channel [S28]. DHS's older guidance puts the adult wait at 5 or more years [S29]. A parent-advocacy site cites about 44 months as of March 2025, and a third-party guide estimates about 16,500 on the list. Neither reconciles with DHS's count, so the current wait length is not claimed [S30].

**Ligas consent decree.** The FY2026 Ligas plan commits to a minimum of 630 people entering service each year and a 60-month maximum PUNS wait [S33]. As of 6/30/2025, 15,433 class members had been selected from PUNS and 8,794 had received waiver capacity award letters [S32]. The class totaled 21,737 at the end of FY25, of whom 19,887 were living at home [S32]. DDD received 181 crisis requests in FY25 and 4,278 cumulatively since the Decree [S32]. The Court Monitor said it cannot yet determine whether selected class members actually received community-based services [S34].

**CILA's share.** The CILA log shows **10,896 people in CILA** at 6/30/2025, of whom 9,762 are in 24-hour settings [S32]. Among Ligas class members, 1,559 have received CILA services versus 7,032 receiving Home Based Services [S32]. **Many families choose to stay at home with supports.** The waiting list overstates demand for a residential bed, and the share of selected people who want a CILA is not published.

**Referral channels for a new home.** The verified channels are ISC agencies, PUNS selection and crisis placements. The referral mix, ICF/DD transitions and CILA vacancy rates were not found (see not_claimed). Existing CILA providers are listed on DHS's provider directory (last updated 07/15/2026) [S45]. The directory is useful for market scanning and partnership outreach, but the provider count was not verified.
sections.operations:
**Staffing rule.** Part 115 requires that anyone responsible for the care of individuals be **physically on-site all hours the individuals are present, unless the individual's Personal Plan says otherwise** [S3][S53]. A 24-hour home therefore needs staff on site around the clock for residents who need 24-hour service [S55]. **No licensure staffing ratio was found in Rule 115.** The ratio tables found are funding definitions in DDD rate bulletins. For example, awake overnight staff do not sleep during the shift for rate purposes [S16]. The model therefore uses an operator-estimated coverage level: one awake staff 24/7 (730 hours/month) plus added hours by home size. Hours per home are 1,220 for 4 residents, 1,830 for 6 and 2,440 for 8. **Verify coverage against each Personal Plan and the staffing assumptions in your rate letter.**

**Training and checks.**
- A criminal background check is required before hire and annually after that [S5].
- The agency may not employ someone until it has queried the applicable registry, and the inquiry may not be more than 30 calendar days before the first day of employment [S3].
- Anyone providing direct care more than 20% of the time must complete DSP training [S5].
- First aid/CPR and OIG Rule 50 abuse and neglect training renew every two years [S5].
- The medication-administration training hours were not confirmed from a current source (see not_claimed).

**Required roles.**
- **Nurse:** the agency must have an RN with a current unencumbered Illinois RN license who completes the DHS/DDD nurse-trainer training [S5]. The model includes 3 RN hours per resident per month (operator estimate).
- **Administrator/leadership:** the application names the owner(s), authorized representatives, officers or administrator for fingerprint checks [S5]. IDHS pages list QIDP, Residential Services Director and Executive Director requirements, but their text was not retrieved (see not_claimed). Confirm the education and experience requirements with BALC before you hire or assign yourself.

**Systems.** Enrollment and billing run through IMPACT [S27]. DDD requires EVV for providers enrolled in IMPACT who bill DDD for personal care or home health care services. From April 1, 2026, providers must keep quarterly EVV compliance above 75% to remain DDD providers [S24][S25]. The verified EVV scope covers Personal Care Services and Home Health Care Services only. **Whether 60D CILA residential claims are subject to EVV is unverified** [S25]. Ask DDD in writing. If EVV applies, the State EVV solution is free, and a third-party system must still send data to HHAeXchange [S25][S26].

**Site and safety.** BALC inspects every new site before occupancy, and OSFM fire clearance is part of the process [S3][S5]. Host family sites need a licensed driver with at least minimum state auto insurance [S3]. The agency's own insurance minimums (liability, professional, property, bond) were not found in the Part 115 text retrieved, so insurance in the model is an operator estimate.
sections.market_conditions:
**Supply.** The CILA log shows 10,896 people in CILA statewide [S32], and DHS publishes a provider directory last updated 07/15/2026 [S45]. **The number of licensed CILA agencies, market shares, named competitors and occupancy rates were not verified**, so this report does not estimate them. A new agency should pull the directory, map providers in its target counties and call a sample to ask about vacancies.

**Price context.** CILA is paid by the waiver, not by residents. The only private-pay benchmark is the Genworth/CareScout 2024 median for an Illinois assisted living community: $5,836/month ($70,032/year, $192/day) [S35]. That survey measures assisted living communities, not CILAs, and is shown for reference only. By comparison, the DDD floor rates are $129.00/day statewide and $147.00/day in Chicago Metro [S19], and the average rates are far higher [S15][S17].

**Wages.** Illinois's 2026 adult minimum wage is $15.00/hour [S36]. Chicago's rises to $17.05 on July 1, 2026 per the City of Chicago, and suburban Cook County is $15.40 [S36][S37]. Chicago's minimum adjusts each July 1 by the lesser of CPI or 2.5% [S37]. **Illinois OEWS wage rows for DSPs, LPNs and managers were not retrieved** [S43]. The model therefore uses an operator-estimated DSP wage of $18.00/hour ($19.00 for the Chicago stress test). Both are above the applicable minimums but are not sourced Illinois wages. The RN wage line uses the national BLS mean ($101,420/year, May 2025, about $48.76/hour) [S42], not an Illinois wage; the Illinois RN median is about $46.15/hour per CareerOneStop. **HB2788** as introduced would require wages of 150% of the applicable minimum wage for DD residential and day staff, and its enactment is not confirmed [S51].

**Real estate.** The only verified rent anchor is HUD's FY2026 two-bedroom Fair Market Rent for the Chicago-Joliet-Naperville area, $1,781 [S60]. HUD defines FMR as a 40th-percentile gross rent [S44]. No metro-wide 4-bedroom figure or commercial survey was verified. Model rents ($3,000 for a 4-bedroom, $4,000 for a 5–6 bedroom, $5,500 for a 7–8 bedroom, $6,500 for the Chicago-area large home) are operator estimates. Rent is fixed whether beds are full or not.

**Employer costs.** Illinois applies unemployment tax to the first $14,250 of wages at a new-employer rate of 3.35% per one pair of secondary sources [S38][S39]. Other secondary sources list different 2026 figures, and the IDES primary page was not fetchable. Workers' compensation is mandatory, and carriers set their own rates under open rating [S58][S59]. Paid leave (Illinois and Chicago) and overtime are real employer costs that are not modeled. An Illinois LLC pays $150 to file and a $75 annual report fee [S40][S41], with no separate LLC franchise tax [S40].
sections.financial_narrative:
**How the P&L is built.** Revenue per resident = the 24-hour CILA daily rate × 30.42 days + $600/month room and board collected from the resident. Rates are the DDD 6/30/2025 average toplines by house capacity: $384.10/day for 4-bed, $355.99 for 6-bed and $336.46 for 8-bed [S17]. The default 6-person home earns about $11,429 per occupied bed per month. At the 90% default occupancy that is about $61,700/month. Costs are driven by (1) **DSP coverage hours** at an operator-estimated $18.00 wage with 22% burden (9% payroll tax, 5% workers' comp, 8% benefits), (2) fractional QIDP, administrator and office staff, (3) an RN at 3 hours per resident per month, and (4) fixed home costs (rent, utilities, vehicle, insurance, maintenance). Food, supplies and billing software scale per resident. Nearly every cost line is an operator estimate, because Illinois wage rows, rent surveys and insurance minimums were not found (see not_claimed). Paid leave and overtime are not modeled, so real costs are higher than shown. The model also does not include any assumption that rates, hours or wages are better than the sourced benchmarks.

**Results at the size-specific average rates (90% occupancy).** The figures below are approximate recomputations after the rate correction; the model's startup cash needs and first-profit months must be regenerated and are not stated here.
- **6-person home (default):** net about **$1,000/month, about 1.6% margin**; break-even occupancy about 88%. The home is only marginally profitable at the 90% default.
- **8-person home:** about **-$3,200/month (about -4%)**; break-even occupancy about 94%. At the 8-bed average rate the home loses money at 90% occupancy.
- **4-person home:** about $2,400/month, about 5%; break-even about 85%. This is only about 5 points of occupancy below the 90% default, so one vacant bed for a few months can erase the profit.
- **Three 4-person homes (12 residents):** about $5,300/month, about 4%; break-even about 86%. Each home needs its own lease and 24/7 coverage, so scale does not help much.

**Floor-rate stress tests are decisively negative.** At the statewide floor of $129.00/day, a 4-person home loses about **$13,066/month** (margin about -80%), and break-even occupancy is about 173%, meaning it cannot break even at any occupancy. At the Chicago Metro floor of $147.00/day, an 8-person home with $19.00 wages and Chicago-area rent loses about **$15,268/month** (about -42%; break-even about 133%). These are the lowest rates on file, and DDD says actual rates are usually higher [S19]. They show that a home populated by residents with low individually determined rates will not work. Profit therefore depends on rate letters near or above the size-specific averages, which this report cannot verify.

**Sensitivities (6-person default).**
- **Rate:** each $10/day change in the average rate moves net by about $1,650/month at 90% occupancy. The 6-bed average already sits below the all-size 24-hour average of $134,395/year (about $368/day) [S17], and the size-specific averages predate the 1/1/2026 DSP wage increase, so actual rate letters may be higher or lower.
- **Occupancy:** break-even is about 88%, so the home is profitable at the 90% default but not at the 85% conservative case. Adult PUNS selections happen annually [S28], so refilling a vacated bed can take months.
- **Wage mandate:** if HB2788 were enacted and DSP wages had to reach 150% of the $15.00 minimum ($22.50/hour), DSP cost would rise by about $10,000/month including burden. The home would then lose about $9,000/month unless rates rise equally [S51]. Its status is unverified.
- **Chicago wage floor:** if a home is in Chicago, a $17.05 minimum [S36][S37] leaves little room above the $18.00 modeled wage. The Chicago stress test models $19.00. DSP wage is the single largest cost. Recompute with local pay quotes, plus paid leave and overtime.

**Ramp and cash.** The model admits one resident per month (two at opening for the 8-person home, four for the multi-home model). Enrollment steps cannot begin until BALC issues a provisional license [S5], so no Medicaid revenue arrives until the first admission. The agency must be operational within 18 months [S7]. Cash needs equal startup costs plus the modeled ramp-up deficit; they are modeled figures, not quotes, and they rise now that revenue is lower for the 6- and 8-bed homes.

**Path to profit.** At the corrected rates the 4-person home has the widest modeled margin, and every profitable configuration needs more than about 85% occupancy. The practical levers are: (1) secure rate letters for residents before you sign a lease; (2) fill beds quickly through ISC agencies and crisis placements; (3) have the owner fill the administrator or QIDP role where qualifications allow; (4) keep DSP overtime and agency staffing low; and (5) start with one home before adding sites.
sections.risks:
**Rate risk (highest).** 24-hour CILA rates are individually determined [S19]. The gap between the $129.00–$147.00 floors and the $336–$384/day size-specific averages [S17][S19] is very large, and the model loses money at the floors. At the 8-bed average the home already loses money at 90% occupancy, and the 6-bed home barely breaks even. A resident with a low rate can make a bed unprofitable. The size-specific averages predate the 1/1/2026 DSP wage increase, and the waiver-wide $375.11 average [S15] has not been shown to match posted rates. Budget risk adds to this: a legislative resolution cites a FY26 $11.2 million CILA funding cut with an unverified outcome [S52], the FY27 proposal reportedly adds no overall regular CILA increase [S50], and the 01/01/2027 waiver amendment is only proposed [S14].

**Wage and labor risk.** Wages are 'operator estimate' values because Illinois OEWS rows were not retrieved [S43]. The Chicago minimum wage is $17.05 from 7/1/2026 per the City of Chicago [S36][S37]. It rises each July 1 [S37]. Paid leave (Illinois and Chicago) and overtime for 24/7 coverage are not modeled and add cost. HB2788 would require 150% of minimum wage and its status is unverified [S51]. DDD requires wage pass-through certification [S47]. Turnover raises training, background-check and overtime costs [S5][S3].

**Licensing risk.** Failing the initial interview or policy review bars reapplication for one calendar year [S5]. The agency must be operational within 18 months or the licensure process is treated as abandoned [S7]. The license term is unclear: 3 years per guidance [S5] versus a two-year licensure period in the rule text [S3] and a pending 2026 bill to shorten it [S13]. Rule 115 has been amended [S46], so use the current text. The proximity rule and its waiver must be handled before leasing [S8]. Unannounced surveys happen at renewal and for complaints [S4].

**Billing and compliance risk.** The EVV status of 60D claims is unverified, and DDD requires EVV compliance above 75% quarterly for covered services [S24]. IMPACT enrollment must be complete before reimbursement [S27]. The managed care versus fee-for-service question is unresolved (see not_claimed). The federal $750 fee may or may not apply [S61].

**Occupancy and demand risk.** Selections are annual [S28], and many selected people choose home-based services over CILA (1,559 vs 7,032) [S32]. CILA vacancy rates are unknown. The Court Monitor said it cannot yet confirm that selected class members actually received services [S34].

**Cost risk.** Rent, insurance and utility figures are operator estimates. No insurance minimums were found in Part 115. Workers' compensation rates vary widely across sources [S58][S59]. Local zoning was not researched. Room-and-board income depends on resident income and no official CILA amount was verified [S22][S23].
sections.recommendations:
1. **Treat the 4-person home as the lowest-risk planning case, and the 6-person home as marginal.** At the corrected size-specific average rates, approximate recomputation shows the 4-person home netting about $2,400/month (about 5%, break-even about 85%) with the lowest capital need. The 6-person home (the model default) nets only about $1,000/month (about 1.6%, break-even about 88%). The 8-person home loses about $3,200/month at 90% occupancy and should not be pursued at the average rate. Three separate 4-person homes (about 4%) are not a good first step. Regenerate the model's cash-need and first-profit-month figures before committing capital.

2. **Do not commit to a lease until you have rate evidence.** Ask DDD and the ISC agencies about the 24-hour CILA rate determinations for people actually seeking placement. The model loses about $13,000–$15,000/month at the floor rates [S19]. Avoid a home whose residents' rates are near the floor. Confirm against a rate letter or the DDD CILA Estimated Rate Calculator, because the size-specific averages [S17] predate the 1/1/2026 DSP wage increase and the $375.11 waiver-wide average [S15] is not specific to home size.

3. **Treat the licensing steps as the real startup work.** Attend the New Provider Orientation if required [S10], request the application from BALC after eligibility is verified [S12], and invest in the policy package, two-year budget, sample case files and implementation strategies. A failed interview means a one-year wait [S5]. Confirm which BALC email is current [S1][S11].

4. **Sequence the property work.** File any proximity waiver **before** you lease, buy or take possession [S8]. Check municipal zoning first. Plan for the BALC pre-occupancy inspection and OSFM fire clearance [S3][S5]. Keep the 18-month operational deadline visible [S7].

5. **Staff the owner role.** Where qualifications allow, the owner or a partner fills the administrator and/or QIDP role to stretch the thin margin. Confirm QIDP and director qualifications with BALC before assuming this [S5].

6. **Replace estimates with quotes.** Get local DSP wage data and pay quotes (compare with the $15.00 statewide and $17.05 Chicago minimums [S36][S37]), liability and workers' comp quotes, local rent, and the cost of paid leave and overtime. Rerun the model at the actual wage. If you operate in Chicago, use the Chicago-wage numbers.

7. **Settle the open compliance questions in writing.** Ask DDD (a) whether 60D claims require EVV [S24][S25], (b) whether billing is FFS through IMPACT or through managed care, (c) whether the IMPACT application fee applies [S27][S61], and (d) the license term and renewal fee [S5][S6][S13].

8. **Capitalize for the ramp and plan for delay.** Hold the modeled cash need for your configuration plus a cushion, because no Medicaid revenue arrives before the first admission [S5] and annual selections can slow fill [S28]. Open one home, reach 90% occupancy, then consider a second.

9. **Watch policy moves.** Track HB2788 [S51], HB5471 [S13], the proposed 01/01/2027 waiver amendment [S14], the FY2027 appropriation [S48][S49][S50] and the Rule 115 amendment text [S46]. Any of them could change your rates, wages or license term.

checklist.task: Confirm the pathway: a CILA license from IDHS BALC, followed by Medicaid waiver enrollment
checklist.instructions: Illinois small-group residential care for adults with developmental disabilities is the Community Integrated Living Arrangement (CILA). Step one is a CILA license from the Bureau of Accreditation, Licensure and Certification (BALC). Medicaid waiver enrollment through DDD/IMPACT comes after the license. Do not start with Medicaid enrollment, and do not apply under an assisted-living or other license type. Agencies planning to develop CILAs must be licensed under Part 115.

checklist.task: Read the CILA Act and the full text of 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115 before spending money
checklist.instructions: Read both documents free on the ILGA/JCAR sites. The Act is 210 ILCS 135. Part 115 is the licensure and operating standard; its stated intent is uniform direction for licensure and operation of CILA agencies. Note that IDHS reports the amended Rule 115 is adopted and in effect. It adds person-centered planning and conflict-free case management, and the effective date is not stated on the page. Allow 1–2 days for reading.

checklist.task: Understand the 8-resident ceiling and design your home around it
checklist.instructions: A CILA is a residential setting or site certified by the Department where 8 or fewer people with a developmental disability live together under agency supervision. Do not plan a site above 8 beds. The bundle model covers 4-, 6- and 8-person homes and a three-home agency.

checklist.task: Form your legal entity (Illinois LLC recommended)
checklist.instructions: File Articles of Organization (Form LLC-5.5) with the Illinois Secretary of State; the fee is $150 per a secondary source. Your application will need owner(s), authorized representatives, registered agent and officers or administrator identified, because the IDPH fingerprint check covers those people. Online filing usually takes days (operator estimate).

checklist.task: Calendar the Illinois LLC annual report ($75)
checklist.instructions: A secondary source gives a $75 annual report fee (Form LLC-50.1) and no separate LLC franchise tax. The late-penalty figure conflicts across secondary sources ($100 vs $300 plus $100/month), so confirm with the Secretary of State and file on time. The model carries about $6/month.

checklist.task: Understand the 1.5% replacement tax if the LLC is taxed as a partnership
checklist.instructions: A secondary source states that LLCs taxed as partnerships pay a 1.5% personal property replacement tax on net income, separate from the annual report fee. It is not modeled in the bundle P&L. Ask your CPA how it applies to your structure.

checklist.task: Obtain a federal EIN and open a business bank account
checklist.instructions: Apply free at irs.gov; the EIN is issued immediately online. Keep the CILA business funds separate from personal funds, and separate again from any resident funds you handle. The IMPACT document list was not retrieved, so confirm which tax and banking documents IMPACT asks for at enrollment.

checklist.task: Capitalize the business for a long pre-revenue period
checklist.instructions: No Medicaid revenue arrives until the first admission, and enrollment steps cannot start until BALC issues a provisional license. The bundle model's total cash needed from startup through break-even is about $84,539 for one 4-person home, $178,346 for one 6-person home (default), $246,970 for one 8-person home and $296,370 for three 4-person homes. These are modeled results based on operator-estimate costs. Arrange cash or a credit line before you apply, and use the 90-day pre-opening spend in the startup tab to refine the figure.
checklist.cite: Bundle financial model; IDHS New Provider Guidance

checklist.task: Buy workers' compensation insurance (mandatory) and get liability quotes
checklist.instructions: Illinois requires all employers to carry workers' compensation. Illinois is an open-rating state, so carriers set their own rates and published advisory figures are only reference points. Secondary sources conflict on average rates ($2.05–$6.42 per $100 payroll), so get at least three quotes. The bundle uses 5% of payroll as an operator estimate.

checklist.task: Obtain general and professional liability, auto, and property coverage
checklist.instructions: No agency liability, professional, auto, property or surety minimum was found in the Part 115 text retrieved, so ask BALC at your orientation or interview whether any minimum applies. Until BALC answers, get quotes from carriers experienced in I/DD group homes. The model uses $450–$900/month per home as an operator estimate.

checklist.task: Register as an Illinois employer for unemployment insurance and withholding
checklist.instructions: Illinois applies unemployment tax to the first $14,250 of wages per employee in 2026 per one secondary source, and the new-employer standard rate is 3.35% per another. Both conflict with other secondary sources (wage base $13,590 or $13,271; rates 3.175%, 3.525% or 3.95%). Confirm your actual rate on your IDES notice. The model uses a 9% payroll-tax load as an operator estimate.

checklist.task: Understand how CILA rates work before you commit: rates are individually determined
checklist.instructions: CILA funding runs through the rate methodology DDD designates (the Guidehouse methodology, with staffing formulas effective 7/1/2024). The 24-hour CILA rate is individually determined for each person, not one fixed rate. The lowest 60D rates on file as of 1/1/2026 are $129.00/day statewide and $147.00/day in the Chicago Metro region. The 2026 waiver amendment lists an average 24-hour daily rate of $375.11, up from $364.50. Treat the average as an average, not a promise.
checklist.cite: DDD Rate Table eff. 1/1/2026; CILA rate methodology

checklist.task: Run the bundle P&L at the floor rate and at the average rate before signing any lease
checklist.instructions: At the average rate the bundle shows: 6-bed home about $4,143/month net (6.4% margin, break-even occupancy 83.9%); 8-bed about $5,304 (6.1%, 84.2%); 4-bed about $1,387 (3.2%, 86.9%); three 4-bed homes about $2,298 (1.8%, 88.3%). At the floor rate the 4-bed home loses about $13,066/month and the 8-bed Chicago home loses about $15,268/month. Margins are thin, and staffing and rent are operator estimates, so replace them with local quotes.
checklist.cite: Bundle financial model; DDD Rate Table

checklist.task: Review the DHS CILA provider list for your region
checklist.instructions: DHS publishes a CILA provider list for intellectual disability services (last updated 07/15/2026). Use it to identify existing agencies for partnership, acquisition or subcontract options. No official provider count or occupancy data was verified, so do not assume market shares.

checklist.task: Size demand from the PUNS snapshot
checklist.instructions: DHS's 7/1/2026 PUNS snapshot shows 8,985 adults (18+) in the Seeking Services category, 1,885 in Planning, and 6,367 eligible for adult waiver selection. Adult selections happen once a year, and enrollment in PUNS does not guarantee services. Treat this as deep but slow-moving demand. The wait length is not verified (older guidance said 5+ years; an advocacy site cites about 44 months as of March 2025).

checklist.task: Read the Ligas data report for how admissions actually flow into CILA
checklist.instructions: As of 6/30/2025, the CILA log shows 10,896 people in CILA, 9,762 of them in 24-hour settings. Among Ligas Class Members, 1,559 had received CILA services versus 7,032 receiving Home Based Services. The Ligas FY2026 plan commits to at least 630 people entering service each year. Use these to size your realistic admission ramp, not as guaranteed referrals.
checklist.cite: Ligas Data Report as of 6/30/2025; Ligas Annual Report 1/27/26

checklist.task: Attend the BALC New Provider Orientation (unless exempt)
checklist.instructions: Attendance at an orientation session is required before certain prospective providers can request the CILA licensure packet. Check the IDHS exemption requirements page to see whether you qualify for an exemption, and keep your attendance proof for the application.
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Orientation Exemption Requirements

checklist.task: Request the application from BALC after eligibility is verified
checklist.instructions: The application is released only after BALC verifies eligibility, and you request it from BALC by email. BALC is at 401 S. Clinton, 7th Floor, Chicago, IL 60607, 312-814-5310. Two IDHS pages list different email spellings (DHS.BALC@illinois.gov and dhs.balc@illinois.gov), so email both or confirm by phone.

checklist.task: Ask BALC for the current qualifications for administrator, QIDP, Residential Services Director and Executive Director
checklist.instructions: These roles are listed on IDHS pages, but the education, experience and training-hour text was not retrieved. Get the current written requirements from BALC before you hire or name anyone, since the model budgets part-time QIDP, administrator and office staff at operator-estimate salaries.

checklist.task: Track pending bills and budget items that could change your economics
checklist.instructions: HB5471 (introduced 2/13/2026) would shorten the CILA license term from 3 to 2 years; its status is unverified. HB2788 as introduced would require wages at 150% of the minimum wage for DD residential staff; enactment is unverified. HJR0044 cites a $11.2M FY26 CILA funding cut; the outcome is unverified. Recheck ilga.gov each quarter.

checklist.task: Complete the application package and pay the $200 nonrefundable fee
checklist.instructions: Submit the CILA application to BALC with the required documents and the $200.00 nonrefundable application fee. The statute caps the application fee at $200. The fee is paid when the package is submitted, not later.

checklist.task: Complete the IDPH electronic fingerprint background check for owners and key officers
checklist.instructions: The application step includes a current electronic fingerprint check, run through the Illinois Department of Public Health, for the owner(s) and/or authorized representatives, the registered agency, and the officers or administrator. Schedule it early and plan for a fingerprint vendor fee (the bundle budgets $100–$300 as an operator estimate).
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: Prepare for and pass the initial BALC interview
checklist.instructions: After your application is approved you must pass an initial interview. If you do not pass it you may not reapply for one calendar year. Prepare owners and the proposed administrator and QIDP on Part 115, person-centered planning and your operating plan, and consider a practice session with an experienced CILA consultant (cost is an operator estimate).
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: Write the policies and procedures manual
checklist.instructions: After passing the interview you must submit policies and procedures. If you fail the policy review you may not reapply for one calendar year. Build the manual to Part 115 section by section, including person-centered planning, conflict-free case management, abuse/neglect reporting, staff training and background checks. The bundle budgets $2,000–$8,000 for policies, budget and sample records combined (operator estimate).
checklist.cite: 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115; IDHS New Provider Guidance

checklist.task: Prepare the projected two-year budget
checklist.instructions: A projected two-year budget is required after the interview. Build it from the bundle P&L for your chosen configuration. Use the average-rate case only if you can show rate support, and show the floor-rate case as a sensitivity. Do not understate required costs (administrator, QIDP, RN, vehicle, insurance) to make it look profitable.
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: Prepare sample case files and sample implementation strategies
checklist.instructions: BALC requires sample case files and sample implementation strategies with your submission. Build redacted or fictional files showing intake, Personal Plan, implementation strategies, progress notes and incident documentation consistent with Part 115. Check the current rule text for the required content.

checklist.task: Build person-centered planning and conflict-free case management into your policies
checklist.instructions: The amended Rule 115, now in effect per IDHS, adds person-centered planning and conflict-free case management. Make sure your policies and forms match the amended rule rather than older templates. Older BALC documents found were dated and should not be used as current requirements.

checklist.task: Understand the provisional license and its limits
checklist.instructions: Upon completion of the application process the Department may issue a provisional license for up to one year, covering one site serving up to eight people. Plan your first site accordingly. Expansion to additional sites comes later.

checklist.task: Start the 18-month operational clock and track it
checklist.instructions: CILA agencies must be operational within 18 months or the Department will consider the licensure process abandoned. Set internal milestones for the license, site, inspections, IMPACT enrollment and first admission, and ask BALC in writing how it measures the 18 months.

checklist.task: Ask BALC for current processing times
checklist.instructions: No current BALC processing time for application review or the initial interview was found in the rule text, so ask BALC directly and build your lease and hiring timeline around the answer. The only verified timing items are the 15-working-day site inspection window and the six-month post-admission site visit.

checklist.task: Check the Rule 115.310 proximity limit before choosing a home
checklist.instructions: A new provider-owned or provider-controlled site may not be next to, across from, diagonal to, or immediately behind another Medicaid HCBS waiver-funded residential or day site owned by the same provider unless a waiver is granted. IDHS says the older 800-foot spacing rule no longer applies broadly and that the limit now targets provider-controlled CILAs. Map each candidate address against your other sites.

checklist.task: File any proximity waiver request before you lease, buy or take possession
checklist.instructions: A proximity waiver request must be submitted before the agency leases, purchases or takes possession of the property. Use the IDHS proximity requirement and waiver page for the process. Add a lease contingency tied to waiver approval if you need one.

checklist.task: Respect the 25% building cap if you consider a multi-unit building
checklist.instructions: No more than 25% of the total units in each building may be CILAs funded by the Department and owned or controlled by CILA providers. Check this before signing for any apartment or condo building.

checklist.task: Confirm local zoning and building-code rules with the municipality
checklist.instructions: Zoning and building codes vary by municipality, and no state-level zoning standard beyond Rule 115.310 was found. Call the local planning and building departments with your address, number of residents and use description, and get the answer in writing before you sign a lease.

checklist.task: Budget the lease realistically and keep rent fixed in the model
checklist.instructions: The bundle models rent as a fixed cost (about $3,000 for a 4-bedroom, $4,000 for a 5–6 bedroom, $5,500 for a 7–8 bedroom, and $6,500 for a large Chicago-metro home) as operator estimates. The only verified anchor is HUD's FY2026 Chicago-metro 2-bedroom Fair Market Rent of $1,781 (a secondary source). HUD defines FMR as a 40th-percentile gross rent. Get local broker quotes for homes with enough bedrooms. Vacant beds still cost rent.

checklist.task: Plan the lease or purchase around licensing contingencies
checklist.instructions: Do not occupy the site until BALC has inspected it. Negotiate a lease with start-date and termination contingencies tied to fire clearance and the BALC site inspection, since the site cannot house residents before then. Have an attorney review the lease (cost is an operator estimate).

checklist.task: Request the Office of the State Fire Marshal inspection once the property is ready
checklist.instructions: Notify BALC when your property is ready, and BALC submits a request to the Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM) to place you on the inspection list. Get any corrections done early because the BALC inspection depends on current fire clearances.
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: Pass the BALC pre-occupancy site inspection
checklist.instructions: Before a new site owned or leased by the CILA agency is occupied, BALC must inspect it. Site inspections are to be completed within 15 working days after all necessary documentation, such as current fire clearances, has been received. Send complete paperwork in one package to keep the clock short.

checklist.task: Equip the home for safety and accessibility
checklist.instructions: Install and test smoke and CO alarms, extinguishers and egress per local fire and building rules, and make accessibility modifications for the residents you expect to serve. The bundle budgets $1,000 per home for safety items, $2,000–$15,000 for accessibility, and $6,000 per home for furniture and housewares (all operator estimates).

checklist.task: Arrange agency vehicle(s) and auto insurance
checklist.instructions: Plan one vehicle per home (about $900/month in the model; an accessible van about $1,200 for an 8-person home, operator estimates). For host family settings the rule requires at least state-minimum automobile insurance. For agency vehicles, confirm any BALC requirement and ask your insurer about passenger coverage.
checklist.cite: 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115 (host family auto insurance)

checklist.task: Wait for the provisional license notice before starting DDD enrollment
checklist.instructions: Providers cannot complete enrollment steps until a notice of a provisional license is received from BALC. Keep the notice and send it with your DDD enrollment materials. Plan hiring and rent timing around this gap, since no revenue arrives until admission.
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: Enroll in IMPACT
checklist.instructions: IMPACT is the Medicaid reimbursement system used to enroll agency and Individual Providers, and any federal reimbursement requires enrollment to be completed first. Start the IMPACT application as soon as BALC issues the provisional license notice. Illinois-specific processing time was not found.

checklist.task: Ask whether a Medicaid provider enrollment application fee applies
checklist.instructions: A secondary vendor source gives a federal CY2026 application fee of $750 for institutional providers, but its applicability to Illinois CILA agencies is unconfirmed. The bundle startup range is $0–$750. Ask IMPACT or DDD at enrollment, and pay only what the system actually requests.

checklist.task: Understand the waiver structure and who pays
checklist.instructions: HFS is the state Medicaid agency and IDHS-DDD is the operating agency for the Adults with Developmental Disabilities 1915(c) waiver (version IL.0350.R05.04 effective 1/1/2026). CILA is a waiver service. Whether services are billed fee-for-service through IMPACT or through managed care was not confirmed by an official source, so ask DDD during enrollment.

checklist.task: Obtain the actual rate for each resident before accepting an admission
checklist.instructions: The 24-hour CILA rate is individually determined under the approved methodology, and the posted floors are $129.00/day statewide and $147.00/day Chicago Metro. A regional wage and rate factor applies to CILA and CDS; Chicago Metro covers Chicago and Cook, DuPage, Kane, Lake, McHenry and Will counties. Ask DDD or the ISC agency for each person's rate and run it through your budget before agreeing to admit.

checklist.task: Learn the billing codes and rate components
checklist.instructions: The CILA rate model uses program code 60D for 24-hour and host family CILA and 61H for hourly intermittent CILA. DDD reported an average annualized 24-hour topline rate of $134,395 in its 2025 update. The 2024 update reported an average administration allowance of $13,764 per person per year. The 1-person intermittent CILA rate is $60.48 statewide in the 2026 amendment. Confirm the code-level table with DDD.

checklist.task: Do not treat the $375.11 average as a posted rate
checklist.instructions: The waiver amendment lists a 24-hour CILA average daily rate rising from $364.50 to $375.11. It is an application-document average and sits far above DDD's floor rates, and it is not verified as reflected in the posted rate table. Use it only for the average-rate scenarios, and cross-check against the 2025 average topline of $134,395/year (about $368/day).

checklist.task: Set up the resident room-and-board arrangement
checklist.instructions: Medicaid does not pay room and board, so residents cover it from income, typically SSI. The 2026 SSI federal benefit rate for a single person is $994/month. A secondary source gives an $874/month cap for Supportive Living ($994 less a $120 personal needs allowance), but that is not a CILA amount, and no official CILA figure was verified. The model assumes $600/month as an operator estimate. Confirm the permitted amount and written agreement with DDD or BALC.

checklist.task: Confirm whether EVV applies to your claims
checklist.instructions: DDD requires EVV for IMPACT-enrolled providers billing personal care or home health care services. Whether 60D CILA residential or 61H intermittent claims are subject to EVV was not verified. Ask DDD. If EVV applies, from April 1, 2026 providers must keep quarterly compliance above 75%. The State EVV solution is free, and a third-party EVV system must still send data to HHAeXchange.

checklist.task: Prepare for the wage pass-through certification
checklist.instructions: DDD requires CILA provider agencies to certify that wage increases are passed through to direct care staff. Set up payroll records that let you document the pass-through for each rate increase.

checklist.task: Set up billing, records and accounting systems
checklist.instructions: Choose accounting and payroll software and a records system for Personal Plans, incident reports and billing. The model budgets about $40 per resident per month for records and billing software as an operator estimate. Billing runs through IMPACT, and no mandatory records vendor was found.

checklist.task: Hire or designate the required RN with an unencumbered Illinois license
checklist.instructions: The agency must have an RN with a current unencumbered Illinois RN license, who completes the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars. Verify the license on the IDFPR website before hire. The model uses the national BLS mean RN wage of about $48.76/hour (a non-Illinois figure) at 2–3 hours per resident per month as an operator estimate, so replace it with an Illinois quote.
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: Run a criminal background check before hire and annually
checklist.instructions: Staff must have a criminal background check before hire and again every year after that. Build the annual re-check into your HR calendar and budget the check fees.
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: Query the applicable registry before employment and keep the inquiry fresh
checklist.instructions: The agency may not employ someone until it has queried the applicable registry, and the inquiry may not occur more than 30 calendar days before the first day of employment. Date-stamp each inquiry and file it in the personnel record.

checklist.task: Train direct care staff as Direct Support Professionals (DSP)
checklist.instructions: Anyone who works as direct care staff with individuals more than 20% of the time must be trained as a DSP. Schedule the training before the first admission and record completion dates in each personnel file. The model budgets $3,000–$12,000 for pre-opening hiring and training as an operator estimate.
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: Complete first aid/CPR and OIG Rule 50 abuse and neglect training, renewed every two years
checklist.instructions: Staff must renew first aid and CPR, and OIG Rule 50 abuse and neglect training, every two years. Track expiration dates for each employee and renew before expiry.
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: Confirm current medication administration training requirements with BALC
checklist.instructions: The only medication training hours found (an 8-hour DHS-approved class with an 80% passing score) came from an outdated BALC document. Ask BALC for the current course and certification requirements before staff administer or assist with medications, and set it with your RN trainer.

checklist.task: Schedule on-site staffing to meet the Part 115 presence rule
checklist.instructions: Anyone responsible for care of individuals must be physically on-site for all hours individuals are present, unless an individual's Personal Plan specifies otherwise. For 24-hour service, plan coverage around the clock. No licensure ratio was found in Part 115; the awake-overnight ratio tables are DDD funding definitions in rate bulletins, not licensure ratios. The model assumes one awake staff 24/7 (730 h/month) plus extra hours by size, as an operator estimate. Confirm coverage with BALC.

checklist.task: Set DSP wages above the applicable minimum wage
checklist.instructions: The Illinois adult minimum wage is $15.00/hour statewide in 2026. Chicago's rate is $17.05 from July 1, 2026 per two secondary sources (a third lists $16.20, so confirm with the Illinois Department of Labor), and suburban Cook County is $15.40. Chicago's rate adjusts each July 1 by the lesser of CPI or 2.5%. The model uses $18.00 (statewide) and $19.00 (Chicago) as operator estimates, because Illinois OEWS wage rows were not retrieved. Check the IDES OEWS tables for your area.
checklist.cite: 820 ILCS 105 (Minimum Wage Law); Chicago Minimum Wage Ordinance

checklist.task: Stress-test payroll against a possible 150% minimum wage requirement
checklist.instructions: HB2788 as introduced would set DD residential and day staff wages at 150% of the minimum wage. Enactment is not confirmed. The bundle's 6-bed sensitivity shows DSP cost rising by about $10,000/month at $22.50/hour and the home losing about $5,900/month unless rates rise equally. Keep a reserve and watch the bill.

checklist.task: Define the administrator, QIDP, and office coordinator roles
checklist.instructions: The model carries part-time QIDP, administrator and billing/records staff (for a 6-person home: 0.75, 0.35 and 0.35 FTE) at operator-estimate salaries. Owners often fill the administrator role. Confirm qualifications with BALC first, then post job descriptions and verify credentials before hire.

checklist.task: Build the payroll burden into your pricing and budget
checklist.instructions: The model uses payroll tax 9%, workers' comp 5% and benefits 8% of wages, all operator estimates. Use your actual IDES rate notice and insurance quote once you have them, and re-run the P&L.

checklist.task: Build ISC agency relationships for referrals
checklist.instructions: Individuals enroll in PUNS through an Independent Service Coordination (ISC) agency, which is the intake and referral channel. Contact the ISC agencies serving your counties, introduce your home and its capabilities, and ask how they share provider choice information. The model budgets $150–$300/month for outreach as an operator estimate.

checklist.task: Understand PUNS selection timing and plan a slow ramp
checklist.instructions: PUNS selections for the Adults with Developmental Disabilities Waiver occur annually, and selection is based on cumulative time in the Seeking Services category. Enrollment is not a guarantee of services. The model ramp (one admission per month, two at opening for larger homes) is an operator estimate, and each month of delay adds a month of fixed cost.

checklist.task: Prepare for crisis placements
checklist.instructions: People facing homelessness, abuse or neglect are told to inform their ISC agency as soon as possible and may qualify without waiting for selection. Tell ISC agencies you can take crisis referrals, if your home and staffing allow, and have a fast intake process ready. DDD received 181 Ligas crisis requests in FY25.
checklist.cite: IDHS Understanding PUNS; Ligas Data Report

checklist.task: Complete a Personal Plan and implementation strategies for every resident
checklist.instructions: On-site staffing rules and 24-hour service depend on each individual's Personal Plan. Work with the ISC/case manager so a current plan, matching rate and support level exist before move-in, and verify each plan against Part 115 and the person-centered planning amendments.

checklist.task: Document 24-hour service for each person who needs it
checklist.instructions: Section 115.580 governs 24-hour service. In host family arrangements residents are considered to need 24-hour service, and host families may not leave them alone except as the plan specifies. Write each resident's supervision level into the plan, and train staff on it.

checklist.task: Run the pre-opening readiness review
checklist.instructions: Before the first admission confirm: provisional license in hand, BALC site inspection and OSFM clearance passed, IMPACT enrollment complete, rate letter for the resident, staff trained and background-checked, RN in place, insurance bound. Remember the BALC unannounced visit within the first year after first admission.
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: Set food, household and supply purchasing controls
checklist.instructions: The model carries food ($350) and household/program supplies ($100) per resident per month as operator estimates. Track actual spend per resident and compare it with the model monthly.

checklist.task: Prepare for the BALC unannounced visit within the first year of admission
checklist.instructions: BQM will make an unannounced visit within the first year from the date of your first admission. Keep personnel files, training records, Personal Plans, incident logs and background-check records current and available at all times.
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: Pass the site visit within six months to convert to the permanent license
checklist.instructions: BALC will do a site visit within six months, and if your agency passes the inspection it will issue your permanent license for 3 years. Run a mock inspection before the window, and fix any gaps found.
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: File the renewal application at least 120 days before expiration
checklist.instructions: On notice from the Department, each licensed agency must submit a signed and dated renewal application at least 120 days before the license expires. Calendar this date as soon as the permanent license issues. The renewal fee amount authorized by the statute was not located, so budget a placeholder (the model uses $25/month) and confirm with BALC. HB5471 would change the term to 2 years if enacted, which would change your renewal date.

checklist.task: Expect unannounced surveys at renewal, for complaints and for health and safety
checklist.instructions: The Department conducts unannounced surveys to determine compliance at license renewal as well as to investigate complaints and health and safety concerns. A secondary source says CILA surveys occur every two years and that satisfactory scores are needed to keep licensure. Every site must be inspected at least once during the licensure period.

checklist.task: Keep every site on an inspection-ready schedule
checklist.instructions: All sites must be inspected at least once during the period of licensure. Keep fire clearances, safety checks and home-condition logs current for each site, and do a self-inspection quarterly (operator practice).

checklist.task: Repeat annual background checks and two-year training renewals
checklist.instructions: Run annual criminal background checks for all staff and renew first aid/CPR and OIG Rule 50 training every two years. Keep a master tracker with due dates and alerts.
checklist.cite: IDHS New Provider Guidance — Steps for CILA

checklist.task: Report any ownership change within 60 business days
checklist.instructions: The agency must notify BALC and DDD within 60 business days of any change of ownership. Plan sales, investor additions or restructurings with this deadline in mind, and consult an attorney.

checklist.task: Keep EVV compliance above the DDD threshold if EVV applies to you
checklist.instructions: Starting April 1, 2026, DDD providers must maintain a quarterly EVV compliance rate of higher than 75% to remain DDD providers (for the EVV-covered services). If your claims are EVV-covered, track compliance monthly. Confirm scope with DDD.

checklist.task: Recheck the 2026 rate table and DDD communications each quarter
checklist.instructions: DDD rates took effect January 1, 2026 after CMS approved the waiver amendments. A further proposed waiver amendment is listed with a 1/1/2027 effective date, and ICF/DD rates were still pending CMS approval as of December 2025. Review DDD communications and rate tables each quarter and update your P&L.
checklist.cite: IDHS DDD Communication (12/17/2025); HFS Adults with DD page

checklist.task: Monitor the state budget for CILA funding changes
checklist.instructions: The proposed FY2027 budget includes over $3.2 billion for DDD. A secondary advocacy summary says the final FY2027 budget includes a $0.60/hour DSP increase. Another secondary analysis says the proposed FY27 budget did not add an overall increase to regular CILA funding. The final enacted DDD appropriation was not verified, so confirm rate impacts with DDD before changing wages.

checklist.task: File the Illinois LLC annual report each year
checklist.instructions: File Form LLC-50.1 and pay the $75 fee before the due date to keep the entity in good standing. A lapse could jeopardize your license ownership records. Confirm the due date and any late penalty with the Secretary of State.

checklist.task: Track occupancy against the break-even occupancy for your configuration
checklist.instructions: The bundle model's break-even occupancy at the average rate is about 83.9% for the 6-bed home, 84.2% for the 8-bed, 86.9% for the 4-bed and 88.3% for three 4-bed homes. The default occupancy is 90% (an operator assumption). Track billed-bed days weekly and act early if occupancy falls near the break-even.

checklist.task: Never admit a resident whose rate will not cover required staffing
checklist.instructions: At the statewide floor of $129.00/day the modeled 4-bed home loses about $13,066/month, and at the Chicago floor of $147.00/day the modeled 8-bed home loses about $15,268/month. Get each resident's rate letter and run your own per-resident staffing cost before accepting an admission.

checklist.task: Keep resident funds and room-and-board collections separate and documented
checklist.instructions: Residents typically live on SSI ($994/month in 2026) and Medicaid does not pay room and board. Use written agreements, a separate resident-funds account and monthly reconciliations. Verify the permitted charge with DDD or BALC before setting it.
checklist.cite: HFS Provider Notice 01/21/2026; SSI benefit rate

checklist.task: Re-run the P&L when your real costs arrive
checklist.instructions: Almost every cost line (rent, utilities, insurance, vehicle, salaries) is an operator estimate. Replace each with an actual quote, update the DSP wage from IDES OEWS data, and recompute break-even occupancy and cash needed. Do not cut required costs (RN, administrator, QIDP, insurance) to make the model profitable.

checklist.task: Model Chicago-area wage and rent scenarios if you operate there
checklist.instructions: Chicago's minimum wage is $17.05 from July 1, 2026 per two secondary sources, and it adjusts annually by the lesser of CPI or 2.5%. The Chicago Metro floor rate is $147.00/day versus $129.00 statewide. Keep leadership and field wages from the same geography as your rates, and model rent with local broker quotes.
checklist.cite: Chicago Minimum Wage Ordinance; DDD Rate Table

checklist.task: Plan for expansion only after the first home is stable
checklist.instructions: Each added home needs its own lease, utilities, vehicle and 24/7 coverage, and the modeled three-home agency earns only about $2,298/month net (1.8% margin). Before expanding, confirm the proximity rule, the 25% building cap and the waiver timing, and make sure a first-home track record supports the rate letters you expect.

checklist.task: Keep a risk log for regulatory and funding changes
checklist.instructions: Log items that could change your model: HB5471 (license term), HB2788 (wage floor), HJR0044 (FY26 CILA funding reduction), any new amendment to Part 115, and the pending 1/1/2027 waiver amendment. Review the log at least quarterly and brief your lender and board.
